events.title: CVE-2026-115893 — Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br
events.summary: (vendor/severity tags below are heuristic) Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br_table instruction with more than approximately 256,000 targets so that it has an incorrect conditional branch target. The branch can then jump to arbitrary other code at a user-controlled offset, allowing a user-controlled Wasm module to escape the sandbox on aarch64 engines using the default Cranelift backend. This issue is fixed in versions 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4.

events.title: [CRITICAL] Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
events.summary: (vendor/severity tags below are heuristic) Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.

claims.text: CVE-2026-112900 is rated 9.2 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-112900 being exploited in the next 30 days at under 1%.
A fix for pillow (PyPI) is published in 13.0.0, per GHSA-w889-685w-c8fh.

events.title: CVE-2026-115567 — Tokio is a runtime for writing applications with Rust. In 1.54.0, a race condition between tokio::time::Interval::poll_tick (including .tick
events.summary: (vendor/severity tags below are heuristic) Tokio is a runtime for writing applications with Rust. In 1.54.0, a race condition between tokio::time::Interval::poll_tick (including .tick().await) and the multi-threaded runtime's time driver could drop an internal timer entry without synchronizing with the driver thread that was firing it. The race caused a use-after-free on the timer's waker and task state in safe Rust, which could produce assertion panics, task reference-count corruption, or heap memory corruption. This issue is fixed in 1.54.1.
